newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to demerge shipping arm.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to demerge shipping arm.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Tuesday it had decided to demerge the Statoil Shipping & Maritime Technology (SMT) business area and form a new partnership with the Rasmussen group of Kristiansand in southern Norway.

"This new company aims to be a leading player in integrated ship-based field solutions as well as operations relating to offshore loading, storage vessels and drill ships," the state-owned energy company said in a statement.
It will also transport crude oil, refined products, gas and methanol.

The Rasmussen group will have a 20 percent interest in the new company, with Statoil holding 80 per cent. It will be established during autumn, 1997, and will be headquartered in Stavanger on the west coast of the country.
Statoil said a shareholder agreement will secure the Rasmussen group an active role in the new company.

Assets being transferred to the new company by the Rasmussen group include shuttle tankers Polyclipper and Polyviking, which work on the British and Norwegian continental shelves, the Polysaga storage vessel on Norway's Yme oilfield in the North Sea, and a 50 percent interest in the limited partnership K/S West Producer.

The new company will also acquire 50 percent of Rasmussen Maritime Services (RMS). This management company will meet the new company's requirements for services and personnel related to construction supervision for and maritime management of new vessels, Statoil's statement said.
RMS will continue to be based in Kristiansand.
The new company will control a fleet of 50 ships, including eight owned wholly or partly by the company. The rest will be on charters of varying duration from Norwegian and foreign owners.
Eight newbuildings are also under construction.

"The combination of Rasmussen's long experience in shipping and offshore operations, and Statoil Shipping's experience with shuttle tankers, loading and production systems and supply of multipurpose vessels will make this new company a strong player both in the North Sea and elsewhere," Peter Mellbye, executive vice president in Statoil, said in the statement.
"This company is an example of the continued good collaboration between Norway's traditional maritime industry and the Norwegian offshore sector," he said.
The statement said efforts to bring in a third partner would be pursued jointly by the Rasmussen group and Statoil.
